In 2007 he found a mausoleum on the hillside with the pieces of a carved limestone sarcophagus that had been smashed in antiquity.
legends.when: Died 4 BCE; tomb announced May 2007 CE

origin.text: BBC News, "King Herod's ancient tomb 'found'" (2007)

legends.look_for: The tomb was not at the foot of the hill, where Netzer looked for decades, but half way up the slope: a podium of fine ashlar, with fragments of carved sarcophagi scattered below it.

places.name: Herodium
places.claim: After a search of more than 30 years Ehud Netzer of the Hebrew University announced that he had located the tomb at Herodium. The team found a smashed limestone sarcophagus about 2.5 m long, decorated with rosettes.
places.against: No inscription names Herod; the identification rests on the place, the date and the quality of the mausoleum and sarcophagus, and it has been questioned.

sources.title: BBC News, "King Herod's ancient tomb 'found'" (2007)
Wikipedia, "Herodium"

legends.name: Tomb of Thutmose II
legends.summary: Thutmose II, husband of Hatshepsut, was the last king of Egypt's 18th Dynasty whose tomb was unknown. A British and Egyptian team led by Piers Litherland found a tomb entrance in the Western Wadis near Luxor in October 2022. In February 2025 it was announced that alabaster fragments naming the king prove it is his: the first pharaoh's tomb found since Tutankhamun's in 1922.
legends.when: Reigned about 1493 to 1479 BCE; entrance found 2022 CE; identified 2025

origin.text: BBC News, "Last undiscovered tomb of Tutankhamun dynasty found" (F. Mao, 2025)

legends.look_for: A rock-cut stair and corridor at the foot of a cliff in a side valley, choked with flood debris. Floods had packed the tomb with debris; a blue ceiling with yellow stars, used only for kings, and fragments of alabaster jars with the names of Thutmose II and Hatshepsut identified it.

places.name: Wadi C-4, Western Wadis, Luxor
places.claim: The team located the tomb in the Western Valleys of the Theban necropolis. Part of the ceiling was painted blue with yellow stars, which the field director Piers Litherland notes are found only in kings' tombs.

sources.title: BBC News, "Last undiscovered tomb of Tutankhamun dynasty found" (2025)
Wikipedia, "Tomb of Thutmose II"

legends.name: Grave of Richard III
aka: The king in the car park
legends.summary: Richard III was killed at Bosworth in 1485 and buried without ceremony in the church of the Grey Friars in Leicester. The friary was pulled down at the Reformation and the grave was lost; a story grew that his bones had been thrown in the river. In 2012 archaeologists from the University of Leicester dug in a council car park where old maps placed the church and found his skeleton on the first day.
legends.when: Buried August 1485; found August 2012

origin.text: R. Buckley et al., "'The king in the car park': new light on the death and burial of Richard III in the Grey Friars church, Leicester, in 1485", Antiquity 87 (2013)

legends.look_for: A lost church in a built-up town: map regression, which lays old maps over new ones, said where to trench. The skeleton had a curved spine and battle wounds, a radiocarbon date of the right decades and DNA that matches living relatives in the female line.

places.name: Greyfriars, Leicester
places.claim: Excavation in 2012 found the choir of the friary church and in it a hastily dug grave with the skeleton of a man with severe scoliosis and fatal head wounds. Genetic and genealogical study published in 2014 concluded that the evidence that it is Richard III is overwhelming.

sources.title: R. Buckley et al., "'The king in the car park': new light on the death and burial of Richard III in the Grey Friars church, Leicester, in 1485", Antiquity 87 (2013)
T. King et al., "Identification of the remains of King Richard III", Nature Communications 5 (2014)
Wikipedia, "Exhumation and reburial of Richard III of England"

legends.name: Tomb of Philip II of Macedon
legends.summary: Aigai was the first capital of the Macedonian kings, and its site was forgotten until it was identified with the village of Vergina. In 1977 and 1978 Manolis Andronikos dug into the Great Tumulus there and found royal tombs that had never been robbed, with gold chests, armour and wall paintings. One of them is identified as the tomb of Philip II, father of Alexander the Great.
legends.when: Philip II was murdered in 336 BCE; tombs found 1977 to 1978 CE

origin.text: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, "Archaeological Site of Aigai (modern name Vergina)"

legends.look_for: A great man-made mound raised over older burials, in a cemetery of more than 300 tumuli. Andronikos was convinced the mound hid royal tombs and dug until he reached them.

places.name: Great Tumulus, Vergina (Aigai)
places.claim: UNESCO records that one of the royal tombs in the Great Tumulus is identified as that of Philip II, and that the tombs were discovered in 1977 and 1978. A 2015 study of the cremated bones in Tomb II supports the view that the man is Philip.
places.against: Which tomb is Philip's is still argued: another reading gives him Tomb I and puts his son Philip III in Tomb II.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, "Archaeological Site of Aigai (modern name Vergina)"
T. Antikas and L. Wynn-Antikas, "New Finds from the Cremains in Tomb II at Aegae Point to Philip II and a Scythian Princess", International Journal of Osteoarchaeology 26 (2015)
Wikipedia, "Vergina"

legends.name: Ark of the Covenant
legends.summary: The Hebrew Bible describes the Ark as a gilded wooden chest that held the tablets of the law and stood in the inner room of Solomon's Temple in Jerusalem. It is not mentioned among the things the Babylonians carried off when they destroyed the Temple in 587 BCE, and nothing certain is heard of it again. Later traditions hide it in a cave or carry it to Ethiopia; no claim has ever been open to inspection.
legends.when: Last placed in the Temple before 587 BCE

origin.text: Exodus 25:10-22 describes the Ark; 2 Maccabees 2:4-8 tells of its hiding

legends.look_for: A wooden chest would not survive 2,600 years in most soils. The claims that exist rest on tradition and on access being refused, so there is nothing for a survey to test.

places.name: Temple Mount, Jerusalem
places.claim: The Ark stood in the Holy of Holies of Solomon's Temple on this hill. Jewish tradition is divided on its fate: that it was taken to Babylon, or that King Josiah hid it in the Temple or in chambers under it.
places.against: No excavation is possible on the Temple Mount, and no trace of the First Temple's furnishings has ever been found.

sources.title: Smithsonian Magazine, "Keepers of the Lost Ark?" (P. Raffaele, 2007)
Wikipedia, "Ark of the Covenant"

places.name: Mount Nebo
places.claim: The Second Book of Maccabees says the prophet Jeremiah took the Ark to the mountain that Moses climbed to see the promised land, hid it in a cave and sealed the door, and that the place will stay unknown until God gathers his people again.
places.against: The book was written centuries after the event and is a religious text, not a record; searches on Mount Nebo have found nothing.

sources.title: 2 Maccabees 2:4-8 (King James Version), Wikisource
Wikipedia, "Ark of the Covenant"

places.name: Church of Our Lady Mary of Zion, Aksum
places.claim: Ethiopian Christians have held for centuries that the Ark rests in a chapel at Aksum, brought from Jerusalem by Menelik, son of Solomon and the Queen of Sheba, as the national epic the Kebra Nagast tells. A single guardian monk tends it and no one else may see it.
places.against: No outside scholar has been allowed to examine the object, and the story of Menelik is a medieval legend.
places.wikipedia: Church of Our Lady Mary of Zion

sources.title: Smithsonian Magazine, "Keepers of the Lost Ark?" (P. Raffaele, 2007)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre, "Aksum"

legends.name: Noah's Ark
legends.summary: Genesis says that Noah's ark came to rest "upon the mountains of Ararat" after the flood. Geology finds no trace of a worldwide flood, and scholars read the story as one of a family of Mesopotamian flood myths. Expeditions have still searched Mount Ararat in Turkey since the 19th century, and a boat-shaped formation nearby has been promoted as the ark since 1959.
legends.when: Written down in the first millennium BCE; searches since the 1800s

origin.text: Genesis 8:4 (King James Version), Wikisource

legends.look_for: Boat-shaped outlines are common where rock layers fold into a trough and erode. "Petrified timbers" and "iron brackets" can be tested under a microscope, and at the best known site they are natural minerals.

places.name: Mount Ararat
places.claim: Tradition fixed the "mountains of Ararat" of Genesis, the old kingdom of Urartu, on this single volcano, and ark hunters have reported wood and shapes in its ice since the 1800s.
places.against: No expedition has produced wood of the right age or any structure, and Genesis names a region, not a peak.

sources.title: Genesis 8:4 (King James Version), Wikisource
Wikipedia, "Mount Ararat"

places.name: Durupınar site
places.claim: A Turkish army captain, İlhan Durupınar, picked out the boat-shaped outline in an air force photograph in October 1959. Ron Wyatt and David Fasold later promoted it as the remains of the ark.
places.against: Fasold himself later co-wrote a geological study: the outline is a natural rock structure, and the "iron brackets" and "walls" are weathered volcanic minerals and rock.

sources.title: L. Collins and D. Fasold, "Bogus 'Noah's Ark' from Turkey Exposed as a Common Geologic Structure", Journal of Geoscience Education 44 (1996)
Wikipedia, "Durupınar site"

legends.name: Holy Grail
legends.summary: The Grail comes from the Arthurian romances of the Middle Ages, where it became the cup of the Last Supper. Scholars treat it as a literary creation. Several real cups are now shown as the Grail, of which the agate cup in Valencia Cathedral has the longest paper trail.
legends.when: Medieval romances; Valencia cup documented from 1399 CE

origin.text: Arthurian romances from the late 12th century on

legends.look_for: A relic is tested by its material and its documents. A stone cup can be dated by its style of carving and its mounts by their craft, but nothing can tie any cup to one supper in Jerusalem.

places.name: Valencia Cathedral (Santo Cáliz)
places.claim: The upper part of the Valencia chalice is a cup cut from agate, which an archaeologist who studied it in 1960 judged to be Middle Eastern work of between the 2nd century BCE and the 1st century CE. Church tradition says it was sent from Rome to Huesca in Spain in the 3rd century for safety.
places.against: A cup of the right age and region is not proof of use at the Last Supper; the handles and base are medieval, and the early history is tradition.

sources.title: BBC Travel, "Is this the home of the Holy Grail?" (2018)
Wikipedia, "Holy Chalice"

places.name: Basilica of San Isidoro, León (2014 claim)
places.claim: Two Spanish historians claimed in a 2014 book, Kings of the Grail, that the jewelled Chalice of Doña Urraca in León is the true cup, on the strength of two Egyptian parchments they found in Cairo. Crowds came and curators had to take the cup off display.
places.against: The researchers themselves admit that Europe has some 200 supposed grails; the claim has not been accepted by other scholars.

sources.title: The Guardian, "Crowds flock to Spanish church after holy grail claim" (2014)

legends.name: Lost Peking Man fossils
legends.summary: Skulls and bones of Homo erectus were dug from a cave at Zhoukoudian near Beijing in the 1920s and 1930s. In 1941, with war coming, they were packed in two crates to be shipped to the United States, and they vanished on the way to the port of Qinhuangdao, near the US Marine base of Camp Holcomb. Only casts remain.
legends.when: Excavated 1920s to 1937; lost December 1941

origin.text: L. Berger, W. Liu and X. Wu, "Investigation of a credible report by a US Marine on the location of the missing Peking Man fossils", South African Journal of Science 108 (2012)

legends.look_for: Two wooden footlockers buried in haste in a camp that is now under a city. Old maps and photographs fix where the camp stood; ground radar could look under the tarmac before anyone digs.

places.name: Zhoukoudian (where the fossils were found)
places.claim: Scientific work at the cave site began in 1921 and uncovered the remains known as Peking Man. The site still yields finds and is a World Heritage Site.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, "Peking Man Site at Zhoukoudian"
Wikipedia, "Peking Man"

places.name: Qinhuangdao (former US Marine camp)
places.claim: A former US Marine, Richard Bowen, reported that in 1947 he dug up a box of bones while digging a foxhole at Camp Holcomb in Qinhuangdao and reburied it. Lee Berger and Chinese colleagues investigated in 2012 and judged the report credible.
places.against: The place has not been excavated, and it is one lead among many that have come to nothing since 1941.

sources.title: L. Berger, W. Liu and X. Wu, "Investigation of a credible report by a US Marine on the location of the missing Peking Man fossils", South African Journal of Science 108 (2012)
Wikipedia, "Peking Man"

legends.name: Nuestra Señora de Atocha
legends.summary: The Atocha was a galleon of the Spanish treasure fleet that sank in a hurricane off the Florida Keys in September 1622, on the way home from Havana. Spanish salvors never found her. The American treasure hunter Mel Fisher searched for sixteen years and found the main part of her cargo in 1985, after a long court fight with the State of Florida over who owned it.
legends.when: Sunk 6 September 1622; main cargo found 1985

origin.text: University of South Florida, Florida Center for Instructional Technology, "Florida's Shipwrecks and Treasures"

legends.look_for: A trail of ballast stones, silver bars and coins scattered for miles across sand, because storms broke the hull and dragged it. Towed magnetometers found the iron of her anchors and guns; the trail then led to the main pile.

places.name: Off the Marquesas Keys, Florida
places.claim: The Tierra Firme fleet of 1622 was caught by a hurricane and the Atocha and the Santa Margarita went down, with 380 lives lost. In 1985 the salvager Mel Fisher found the Atocha in the Florida Keys with tons of treasure.

sources.title: University of South Florida, Florida Center for Instructional Technology, "Florida's Shipwrecks and Treasures"
Wikipedia, "Nuestra Señora de Atocha"

legends.name: 1715 Treasure Fleet
legends.summary: Eleven ships of a Spanish treasure fleet bound from Havana to Spain were driven on to the east coast of Florida by a hurricane in July 1715. Spain salvaged much of the cargo at the time. The treasure hunter Kip Wagner found the first of what was left in 1961, and the wrecks gave this stretch of shore the name Treasure Coast.
legends.when: Wrecked 31 July 1715; treasure found again from 1961

origin.text: University of South Florida, Florida Center for Instructional Technology, "Florida's Shipwrecks and Treasures"

legends.look_for: Piles of ballast stones and iron cannon close inshore, in the surf, with coins spread through the sand around them. Storms uncover and bury them; beach finds after storms pointed to each wreck.

places.name: Treasure Coast, Florida (Sebastian to Fort Pierce)
places.claim: All eleven ships of the fleet were lost in a hurricane along the east coast of Florida on 31 July 1715. The Urca de Lima, a flat-bottomed storeship, is the best known of the wrecks.

sources.title: University of South Florida, Florida Center for Instructional Technology, "Florida's Shipwrecks and Treasures"
Wikipedia, "1715 Treasure Fleet"

legends.name: USS Indianapolis
legends.summary: The cruiser USS Indianapolis had just delivered parts of the first atomic bomb when a Japanese submarine torpedoed her in the Philippine Sea on 30 July 1945. Only 316 of her crew survived, many of the rest dying in the water before rescue came. The wreck was found on 19 August 2017 by a team funded by Paul Allen, 5.5 km down.
legends.when: Sunk 30 July 1945; found 19 August 2017

origin.text: BBC News, "Lost WW2 warship USS Indianapolis found after 72 years" (2017)

legends.look_for: A steel warship on abyssal mud, found by an autonomous vehicle with sonar after fresh work in naval records narrowed the search box. The site is a war grave and its position is not published.

places.name: Philippine Sea, between Guam and Leyte (position not published)
places.claim: The ship was found 18,000 feet (5.5 km) under the Pacific, 72 years after she sank somewhere between Guam and Leyte. The civilian search team was led by the Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen.

sources.title: BBC News, "Lost WW2 warship USS Indianapolis found after 72 years" (2017)
Wikipedia, "USS Indianapolis (CA-35)"

legends.name: Battleship Musashi
legends.summary: Musashi and her sister Yamato were the largest battleships ever built. American carrier aircraft sank Musashi in the Sibuyan Sea, in the Philippines, in October 1944 during the Battle of Leyte Gulf. In March 2015 Paul Allen announced that his team had found the wreck on the sea floor after a search of eight years.
legends.when: Sunk October 1944; found March 2015

origin.text: The Guardian / AFP, "US billionaire Paul Allen discovers wreck of Japan's biggest warship Musashi" (2015)

legends.look_for: A very large steel hull broken into pieces on a deep sea floor. Historical records and seabed mapping narrowed the area; an autonomous vehicle and then a remotely operated vehicle with cameras confirmed her by the chrysanthemum crest on the bow.

places.name: Sibuyan Sea
places.claim: Pictures taken on the floor of the Sibuyan Sea by a team from Allen's vessel Octopus showed the bow with the chrysanthemum crest of the Japanese imperial family.

sources.title: The Guardian / AFP, "US billionaire Paul Allen discovers wreck of Japan's biggest warship Musashi" (2015)

legends.name: HMS Hood
legends.summary: The battlecruiser HMS Hood, for twenty years the pride of the Royal Navy, blew up and sank in the Denmark Strait on 24 May 1941 under the guns of the German battleship Bismarck. Of 1,415 men on board, three lived. The wreck was found in 2001, 2,800 m down, and her bell was raised in 2015 as a memorial.
legends.when: Sunk 24 May 1941; found 2001

origin.text: BBC News, "Recovery of HMS Hood's ship's bell abandoned" (2012)

legends.look_for: Wreckage in several large pieces spread over a wide debris field, which itself records how the ship broke up. It was found by deep-sea survey and filmed by a remotely operated vehicle, and it is a protected war grave.

places.name: Denmark Strait, between Greenland and Iceland
places.claim: The deep-sea search company Blue Water Recoveries found the wreck in 2001, 2,800 m under water. The bell was seen lying on the seabed away from the hull, and a first attempt to recover it in 2012 was called off.

sources.title: BBC News, "Recovery of HMS Hood's ship's bell abandoned" (2012)
Wikipedia, "HMS Hood"

legends.name: Bonhomme Richard
legends.summary: Bonhomme Richard was the ship in which John Paul Jones fought HMS Serapis off Flamborough Head, Yorkshire, on 23 September 1779, the most famous sea fight of the American Revolution. Jones won, took the British ship, and watched his own sink a day and a half later. Searches have gone on for decades, and a find announced off Filey in 2018 has not been confirmed.
legends.when: Sank 25 September 1779 CE

origin.text: BBC News, "Remains of USS Bonhomme Richard found off Yorkshire coast" (2018)

legends.look_for: The remains of a burned wooden ship of the 1700s on a seabed crowded with later wrecks and scoured by trawls: iron guns, ballast and concretions. Each candidate needs guns or fittings that can be dated to her French origin.

places.name: Off Filey and Flamborough Head, Yorkshire
places.claim: The land and sea search firm Merlin Burrows announced in December 2018 that it had found the remains of the ship off the coast at Filey, closer inshore than earlier searches had looked.
places.against: No independent body has confirmed the identification, and earlier surveys had pointed to other wreck sites further out off Flamborough Head.

sources.title: BBC News, "Remains of USS Bonhomme Richard found off Yorkshire coast" (2018)
Wikipedia, "USS Bonhomme Richard (1765)"
